features.title: Gateway protocol v4

acceptance_evidence.required: A Rust protocol constant test proves v4 negotiation and rejects unsupported general-client versions.

known_differences: Negotiation is proven in-process against the pinned frame contract; the upstream version constant is mirrored by hand in Rust rather than generated from the frozen source file.

features.title: Gateway node N-1 protocol window

acceptance_evidence.required: Handshake tests prove authenticated node-mode v3 acceptance while general clients remain v4-only.

known_differences: The N-1 window is proven for node and probe client modes at the negotiation layer; no live-socket test drives a v3 node through a complete authenticated session.

features.title: Gateway frames and handshake

acceptance_evidence.required: Golden-frame tests cover connect.challenge, connect, hello-ok, req, res, event, limits, and error cases.

known_differences: Golden frames are asserted as decoded Rust values against hand-transcribed fixtures rather than byte-for-byte against captured upstream traffic.

features.title: Gateway method catalog

acceptance_evidence.required: Generated Rust catalog matches every pinned core method name, scope, and advertised flag.

known_differences: The catalog is a hand-written Rust table cross-checked against the frozen inventory in both directions rather than generated from it; the behaviour of individual method handlers is covered by other rows.

features.title: Gateway event catalog

acceptance_evidence.required: Generated Rust event catalog and event-envelope tests match all pinned events.

known_differences: All pinned event identities and the event-envelope shape are proven; per-event payload schemas are decoded only for the control events tick, shutdown and connect.challenge.

features.title: Gateway roles and operator scopes

acceptance_evidence.required: Authorization matrix tests cover operator, node, worker, and all six closed operator scopes.

known_differences: The matrix restates the expected rule independently of the production resolver and walks every role and scope subset; dynamic-scope catalog entries are resolved by a policy restated in the test because the frozen inventory carries no resolution column.

features.title: Gateway liveness and readiness HTTP probes

acceptance_evidence.required: HTTP tests prove /health, /healthz, /ready, and /readyz status and draining behavior.

known_differences: Status codes, bodies, cache-control and unauthenticated detail hiding are proven for the health and readiness probes.

Draining is not proven over HTTP: readiness is only flipped by a failing dependency, and the daemon drain is observed at process level in apps/gta-claw-daemon/tests/process_shutdown.rs, which never queries these routes.

features.title: Watch-node HTTP transport

acceptance_evidence.required: Transport tests cover challenge, connect, disconnect, long poll, result, authentication, and queue limits.

known_differences: The transport is exercised over real sockets against the in-process server; no separate node binary is driven through the long-poll loop.

features.title: Top-level configuration domains

acceptance_evidence.required: Rust config fixtures deserialize every pinned top-level domain and reject unknown contract-breaking shapes.

known_differences: Every frozen top-level domain deserializes, round-trips without name drift and rejects unknown keys with an exact path; exhaustive field-level coverage below the top level exists only for the domains named in every_frozen_domain_enforces_a_concrete_value_type.

features.title: Context-engine SPI

acceptance_evidence.required: A Rust SPI conformance harness proves bootstrap, ingest, assemble, maintain, and compact lifecycle behavior.

known_differences: The conformance harness proves the documented lifecycle checks against in-repository engines; no third-party context engine has been run through it.

features.title: Commands and directives

acceptance_evidence.required: Command registry and directive parsing golden tests match pinned aliases, authorization, and inline behavior.

known_differences: Directive parsing, inline stripping into turn options, the builtin command registry and per-scope authorization are proven.
Pinned aliases are not proven: the repository has no alias table and no test compares a registry alias set against the frozen upstream command list.

features.title: Durable session goals

acceptance_evidence.required: Restart, compaction, command, model-tool, budget, and status transition tests prove durable goal behavior.

known_differences: Durability is proven by rebuilding the runtime over the same store rather than by restarting a real operating-system process.

features.title: Crestodian setup and rescue

acceptance_evidence.required: Ring-zero tool, typed mutation, rescue grammar, owner-DM, and restart acceptance tests pass.

known_differences: The closed rescue grammar, owner and direct-message gating, same-owner restart approval and typed guided-setup mutation are proven.
The ring-zero tool surface is not proven: the rescue control plane is a library API and no test registers or invokes it as an agent-callable tool, so nothing shows it is reachable from a session.

features.title: Admin HTTP RPC

acceptance_evidence.required: Authenticated POST /api/v1/admin/rpc dispatch tests prove method policy and error mapping.

known_differences: Authenticated dispatch, the supported-method policy, scope denial and error mapping are proven for the admin RPC route; the unauthenticated rejection is covered by the shared HTTP auth layer rather than by a case naming this path.

features.title: Cooperative host suspension

acceptance_evidence.required: Prepare, busy, lease expiry, status, resume, and draining integration tests pass.

known_differences: The controller is driven through an injected clock and synthetic work permits rather than a real host suspend and resume cycle.

features.title: Closed worker protocol

acceptance_evidence.required: Admission, fencing, expiry, RPC allowlist, replay, and payload-limit tests pass.

known_differences: The registry is proven in isolation with an injected clock; the allowlist is a Rust constant asserted against its nine documented method names rather than derived from the frozen gateway method inventory.
